Effects On World  Today - The cold war
Effects on the world
The cold war has many lasting effects on the world today. In the present, America still has an embargo with Cuba, nothing shipped to Cuba, nothing shipped back. Americans are also not allowed to go to Cuba, and with the fall of the Soviet Union, America was established as a world superpower.
Additionally, nuclear arms production sites are still radioactive. Tons of places in the world are affected by the radioactivity, including the air and water. Almost all of the nuclear weapons are still viable , and American/Russian political relations are still strained.
Although the threat of nuclear war and overall paranoia in both countries was bad, the cold war had a few good points, at least for America. For one thing, the threat of communists and their apparent evil helped distract from other social problems, like racism. Discrimination against African-American was second priority, as was inequality for women, so some a little bit of the social problems were remedied. During the Cold War, the government had even gone to the lengths of banning anti-Black laws, but nobody really noticed all that much.

What were the long term effects of the cold war?
The long-term effects of the Cold War on American government were immense. First and foremost, it led to the permanent creation of a peacetime defense and armaments industry, as President Eisenhower noted in his farewell address. It forced the United States to adopt a much more international outlook on world affairs.
How was the economy affected by the cold war?
The U.S. Cold War economic policies were in contrast to those the United States pursued to win World War II. To win the Cold War, the United States became a low-savings, high-consumption economy. It basically supported its allies in a recovery, development and growth process that out-consumed the USSR and China.
What was the outcome of the Cold War?
During 1989 and 1990, the Berlin Wall came down, borders opened, and free elections ousted Communist regimes everywhere in eastern Europe. In late 1991 the Soviet Union itself dissolved into its component republics. With stunning speed, the Iron Curtain was lifted and the Cold War came to an end.
How was Russia affected by the cold war?
After Russia embarked on several economic reformations in the 1990s, it underwent a financial crisis and a recession more oppressive than the United States and Germany experienced during the Great Depression.
What intensified the cold war?
Development of the Hydrogen Bomb While anti-communist tensions were at a moderate baseline in the early years of the Cold War, the period of time encompassing the race to develop a functional hydrogen bomb set the precedent for the rising tensions of the Cold War as it escalated throughout the 20th century.
Why did the Soviet Union suddenly wanted to become better friends with the United States just because China had?
The Soviet leader suddenly wanted to become friends with the United States, because an alliance between China and the United States would be tough to beat. The Soviet Union also wanted to become better acquainted, because they were scared of getting attacked.
